claim: A Sylhet man who took BDT 10 lakh per visa for UK work permit visas sent photos of the visas on WhatsApp; the passports came back by courier with no visa in them
After local mediation he gave six cheques of BDT 2 lakh each, which the bank dishonoured for insufficient funds
Victims said he had sent his own two sisters to England
Refund cheques given by the study-abroad firm BSB Global Network were repeatedly dishonoured by the bank
The complainants' lawyer showed the court photos of the firm's chairman with the former prime minister and ministers
A man who took money for Canada worker visas closed his Jashore office and opened a new one, 'Euro Visa Help Center BD', in Natore
He took BDT 1,500,000 from one victim
Victims of the student-visa firm VisaGuide went to its office on 5 July 2026 and found it had been moved away
The firm had given victims cheques and money receipts
A Barishal man agreed with his neighbour to pay BDT 350,000 for a Dubai job, BDT 200,000 first and the balance after the visa
He was sent to Dubai on a seven-day tourist visa, held by a broker ring there and sent back by Dubai police
When he asked for a refund he was asked for more money to go to Kyrgyzstan instead
A woman going to join her husband in Italy had a written agreement with a Gulshan travel agency that she would pay in full only after the visa was issued
A real Italy visa was issued in her passport, and at Dhaka airport immigration she learned another woman had already travelled to Italy on it on 24 April
She had met the tout outside the Italian embassy
CID seized 56 passports and 153 seals from the ring
People in a Madaripur village went to a broker after his own two sons reached Italy
Two men who each paid him BDT 1,500,000 were promised a ship and put on a small engine boat with about 50 people; they died at sea on 21 October 2025
The families were told 21 days later; before that the broker had said the men were alive
A Madaripur broker was known locally for having sent more than 300 young men to Italy through Libya
Locals said a Libya-based broker from Adityapur, Madaripur, had sent over 50 young men from the village to Italy in one year
A union parishad chairman in Sakhipur, Tangail, took BDT 100,000 each from villagers to send them abroad, collected partly through union parishad members; no visa came in more than six months
Two Madaripur brothers who drowned off Tunisia had been sent by a man who is the local union parishad chairman, according to the family; he denies it
The brokers kept telling the family the brothers were alive and avoided letting them speak by phone; a relative in Italy told the parents about four months later
A Sylhet family made a verbal agreement for Spain with a local political party office-holder; the son was sent to Libya and tortured for more money, and the family paid about BDT 2,500,000 in all
Four Patgram men who paid BDT 900,000 each for jobs in Russia were recruited by local political figures working with a recruiting agency in Uttara, RS International
The agency's office was found locked on 7 June 2026
A Rajbari woman was sent to Cambodia by an employee of the NGO she had borrowed from, who helped her get a BDT 100,000 NGO loan towards the cost
In Cambodia her passport and money were taken

S Alam Overseas, in a flat in Sector 12, Uttara, gave people appointment letters from an Azerbaijan construction company, showed visas, arranged online interviews with foreigners and sent them for a medical test
Victims paid in stages, BDT 80,000 to 350,000 each, and BDT 5,000 for the medical test
On 23 October the receptionist phoned to say the company had closed; the appointment letters and visas were fake
About 200 people were cheated, according to the victims
A father and son in Wari, Dhaka, claimed the licences of four or five recruiting agencies, sent people for a medical test after payment and gave fake appointment letters and visas
A ring took BDT 600,000 for Serbia and handed over a visa; airport immigration police found it was forged
When a visa failed at immigration the ring told the traveller the problem lay elsewhere
